 Brett McMurphy's college football AP Top 25 ballot after Week 9
 Brett McMurphy @ Brett_McMurphy 6h 1 Share Share 
 Miami continued as the No. 1 team on my Associated Press Top 25 ballot as the Hurricanes survived a scare at North Carolina. Entering November, Miami is one of three unbeaten teams, along with UCLA and Utah.
 Despite Georgia having one loss, I kept the Bulldogs at No. 2 behind Miami. UCLA moves up to No. 3 on my ballot after Ohio State’s loss at USC. The remainder of my Top 10: No. 4 Kentucky, followed by Utah, Ohio State, Indiana, BYU, Notre Dame and Ole Miss.
 USC, Missouri and UTSA are new teams on my ballot this week.
 My AP Top 25 ballot after Week 9.
 1. Miami (8-0)
 With next week’s anticipated rematch at Notre Dame , the Hurricanes held on for a 38-35 victory at North Carolina . QB Darian Mensah threw for 274 yards and three TDs, two to WR Malachi Toney , who had seven receptions for 75 yards.
 2.  Georgia (7-1)
 The Bulldogs used a dominating defensive effort to defeat Florida 27-8 in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party, played inside at Atlanta. Georgia intercepted Florida quarterbacks three times and also forced a fumble. The Dawgs had a pick-6 for a TD and had another interception in the end zone. Gunner Stockton only threw for 101 yards, while Nate Frazier and Dwight Phillips Jr. each added 67 yards rushing.
 3.  UCLA (8-0)
 The Bruins blanked  Nevada 27-0, their first shutout at the Rose Bowl since 2007. The Bruins held Nevada to 176 yards and forced four turnovers. UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach threw for 178 yards and a touchdown and ran for another. UCLA’s 8-0 start is its best since the 2005 team started 8-0 and finished with a school record-tying 10 victories.
 4.  Kentucky (7-1)
 The Wildcats did not play last week. Kentucky’s seven wins tie for the most in a season in the past five years. Kentucky puts its six-game winning streak on the line Saturday at Tennessee. The Wildcats haven’t defeated UT since 2020.
 5. Utah (8-0) 
 Any concerns that Utah might be looking ahead to next week’s Holy War with BYU quickly disappeared as the Utes raced to a 36-point halftime lead on their way to an easy 49-25 victory at Cincinnati . QB Devon Dampier threw three touchdown passes and the Utes’ defense scored TDs on an interception and fumble return.
 6.  Ohio State (6-2)
 Playing their first game without injured QB Julian Sayin , the Buckeyes lost at USC 30-18. QB Luke Fahey , making his first start, threw for 260 yards, a touchdown and an interception. WR Jeremiah Smith had 10 catches for 83 yards and a TD. Bo Jackson had a game-high 121 yards rushing on 21 carries.
 7.  Indiana (8-1)
 The Hoosiers survived another close call, outlasting Minnesota 23-16 in overtime. Indiana won its second consecutive OT game and improved to 4-1 this season in games decided by one score. Paddy McAteer’s 60-yard field goal on the final play of regulation sent the contest to overtime. WR Charlie Becker (eight receptions, 149 yards) carried the offense, scoring the game-winning 25-yard TD in OT and setting up McAteer’s field goal in regulation with a 33-yard reception.
 8. BYU (7-1)
 The Cougars beat Arizona State 27-20, rebounding from last week’s upset loss at UCF . BYU QB Bear Bachmeier threw for 236 yards and a TD. Of Bachmeier’s 19 completions, Legend Glasker (87 yards), Kyler Kaspar (57 yards) and Walker Lyons (49 yards) combined for 14 receptions.
 9. Notre Dame (7-1)
 The Fighting Irish shook off a sluggish start to pull away from Navy 35-13. Notre Dame trailed 13-7 late in the second quarter, but scored the game’s final 28 points. RB Nolan James Jr. rushed for 107 yards, including TDs of 52 and 23 yards. QB CJ Carr threw for 210 yards and two scores as the Fighting Irish won their ninth consecutive game against the Midshipmen.
 10. Ole Miss (6-2)
 The Rebels rolled past Auburn 45-15 behind QB Trinidad Chambliss . Leading only 17-15 late in the third quarter, Chambliss ran for a TD and threw for two more in the convincing victory. Chambliss finished with 263 yards passing and 65 yards rushing. Shekai Mills-Knight had 71 yards rushing and a TD and Horatio Fields added six receptions for 73 yards and a TD.
